competitor_summaries.name: Sugar & Slice Karachi
competitor_summaries.positioning_summary: Positions heavily on elaborate, Instagram-first cake design -- homepage and feed are almost entirely photos of intricate custom designs, with pricing and flavor described only in passing.

competitor_summaries.name: The Baking Room
competitor_summaries.positioning_summary: Positions on volume and speed -- same-day and next-day availability is the headline message, with a simpler, more standardized menu than a fully custom bakery.

cross_competitor_patterns: Both competitors lead with visuals (Instagram feed, photo galleries) rather than any statement about flavor or ingredient quality.
Neither prominently mentions sweetness level or ingredient sourcing anywhere in their visible homepage/profile text.
Pricing is not shown upfront on either -- both push toward a DM/inquiry step before revealing cost.

differentiation_angles.angle: Lead with 'balanced sweetness, real ingredients' as an explicit, stated claim rather than an implied one.
differentiation_angles.reasoning: Neither competitor makes any flavor or ingredient claim visible on their own channels -- this is genuinely open space, not a crowded angle, and it's already Velvet Crumbs' real differentiator per the business profile.

differentiation_angles.angle: Show a price range upfront instead of requiring an inquiry.
differentiation_angles.reasoning: Both competitors gate pricing behind a DM, which is a common friction point in this category -- being the one bakery that's upfront about cost could reduce drop-off from price-sensitive but interested customers.

differentiation_angles.angle: Pair design-quality content (matching the category norm) with occasional flavor-focused content (a gap), rather than picking one or the other.
differentiation_angles.reasoning: Competing purely on visuals means competing directly with Sugar & Slice's core strength; adding flavor-forward content plays to an area they don't currently occupy.

caveat: This is based on a light read of each competitor's own homepage/profile text, not a full market study -- it's meant as informed context for your own judgment, not a verdict on what will or won't work.
